pageCache.text:
Welcome to our school
Welcome to our wonderful school, where together, we are bold and courageous learners, guided by God’s love.
Inspired by the words, “Be bold, be strong, for the Lord your God is with you” – Joshua 1:9, we encourage every child to grow in confidence, character and curiosity. We combine a nurturing, inclusive environment with high expectations, because children achieve their God-given potential when they feel safe, valued and that they belong.
I would love for you to see our school in action. If you think Walberton & Binsted might be the right place for your child, please get in touch to arrange a tour.
Joe Neale - Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - French
pageCache.text:
French
At Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School, our French curriculum aims to develop confident language learners who can understand and communicate simple ideas in French, while nurturing curiosity and respect for other cultures. It reflects our vision of becoming bold and courageous learners, broadening children’s horizons and opening doors to the wider world.
Our carefully sequenced curriculum builds knowledge of pronunciation, vocabulary and basic grammar through listening, speaking, reading and writing. Songs, stories, games and conversation provide enjoyable opportunities to practise and revisit learning, helping pupils communicate with increasing independence.
Children are encouraged to speak with courage and see mistakes as part of learning. We want every pupil to leave our school with secure foundations for future language learning, an appreciation of cultural diversity and the confidence and enthusiasm to connect with others.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
At Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School, our music curriculum reflects our vision: “Together, we are bold and courageous learners, guided by God’s love.” We aim to develop confident, creative musicians who have the knowledge and skills to listen thoughtfully, sing, play, compose and perform, alongside a lasting enjoyment of music. Our ambitious and inclusive curriculum enables every child to participate and succeed, whatever their starting point.
Through a carefully sequenced curriculum, pupils build their understanding of pulse, rhythm, pitch, dynamics, tempo and structure. Regular practice and opportunities to revisit learning help children develop their musical skills, use musical vocabulary confidently and reflect on their own and others’ work.
Children explore diverse musical traditions, genres, composers and performers from across the world, broadening their horizons and deepening their appreciation of different cultures. Through shared musical experiences, they develop collaboration, resilience and the courage to express themselves. We want every child to leave our school with the confidence, skills and enthusiasm to enjoy and participate in music throughout their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Parent Partnership and Engagement
pageCache.text:
Parent Partnership and Engagement
At Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School, we see the parent/school partnership as absolutely vital to every child’s success. We are proud to be a Parent Friendly School, where families are not just informed, but actively involved as genuine partners in their child’s education.
Research is clear that strong parental engagement can add the equivalent of four months’ additional progress over the course of a year.
We believe that the strongest partnerships are built on trust, support and shared responsibility. This means creating a welcoming culture, maintaining clear and timely two-way communication, and ensuring that every family feels valued, listened to and included.
We place great importance on communication with parents and carers to ensure that information sharing is timely, purposeful and has the greatest possible impact on a child’s learning, wellbeing and development throughout the year.
At Walberton & Binsted, this commitment is brought to life through everyday practice:
How do I know how well my child is doing?
We send home a written report three times a year. These are shorter update reports in the autumn and spring terms, followed by a more detailed end-of-year report in the summer term.
Reports explain how your child is progressing and whether they are working below, at, or above age-related expectations. Each report also includes a “How can I help my child at home?” section, giving practical ways you can support learning at home.
We also send home diagnostic progress reports from our STAR assessment system in reading and maths, so parents can see exactly where their child is being successful and which areas they need to continue developing.
When can I talk to the teacher?
We hold three parents’ evenings each year, including an optional appointment in the summer term. In addition to this we hold 'Meet the teacher' meetings at the start of each year.
In addition to this, teachers are available to speak with parents whenever needed. Quick conversations can often take place at drop-off or pick-up. For longer conversations, you can arrange a meeting directly with your child’s teacher.
Teachers’ email addresses are shared with parents at the beginning of the year, and parents are encouraged to contact teachers directly if they have a question, concern or would like to arrange a conversation.
We recognise that parents are busy, so we are happy to communicate in the way that works best for everyone, whether face to face, online or by telephone.
How can I see my child’s work?
Several times a year, we hold Learning Look-ins, which give parents the opportunity to come into classrooms, see their child’s work and achievements, and celebrate their learning.
If you would like to see your child’s work at another point in the year, please contact your child’s class teacher. They will be happy to arrange a convenient time for this.
What if I have a concern?
If you are concerned about something relating to your child, the best person to speak to in the first instance is usually your child’s class teacher. They know your child well and are often best placed to understand the situation and agree the right next steps.
In some circumstances, it may be helpful or necessary to speak to another member of staff. Our senior leadership team, SENDCo and pastoral lead are all available to contact as required, and are also easily accessible on the school gate and playground each morning.
In most cases, concerns and worries can be addressed and resolved quickly once they are shared, so we would always encourage parents to get in touch early.
How can I support my child with their learning at home?
Our Home Learning Guide for Parents provides simple, practical suggestions for each year group, including reading, spelling and number practice.
If you can only do one thing, read! Sharing books, enjoying stories and talking about what your child has read can make a real difference.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Science
pageCache.text:
Science
At Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School, our science curriculum reflects our vision: “Together, we are bold and courageous learners, guided by God’s love.” We aim to inspire curiosity, nurture a sense of wonder and equip children with the knowledge and skills they need to understand and explore the world around them.
We believe that science is an essential part of a broad and ambitious curriculum. It encourages children to ask meaningful questions, investigate ideas and use evidence to explain their thinking.
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that pupils build secure scientific knowledge over time. Important concepts are revisited and developed throughout their primary education, helping children to make connections and deepen their understanding. Working scientifically is woven throughout the curriculum, allowing pupils to develop their skills in observing, questioning, predicting, investigating, recording and evaluating.
We have chosen to use Developing Experts to support the teaching of science because it combines a carefully sequenced, knowledge-rich curriculum with practical investigations and meaningful links to the world beyond school. Through Developing Experts, children regularly encounter real scientists, engineers and other STEM professionals who explain how scientific knowledge is used within their work. By seeing people from a wide range of backgrounds applying science in real-life contexts, pupils learn that science is for everyone. These role models encourage children to be bold and courageous in their aspirations and help them imagine the possibilities that a future in science, technology, engineering or mathematics could offer.
We want every child to see themselves as a scientist: curious, knowledgeable and confident enough to investigate challenging questions. By the time pupils leave Walberton & Binsted, we want them to have secure scientific knowledge, strong enquiry skills and a lasting curiosity about the world. Above all, we want them to approach new discoveries with courage, wonder and a lifelong love of learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Art and Design
pageCache.text:
Art and Design
At Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School, our art curriculum reflects our vision: “Together, we are bold and courageous learners, guided by God’s love.” We aim to develop confident, creative artists who have the knowledge and skills to explore ideas, express themselves and appreciate art in its many forms. Our ambitious and inclusive curriculum enables every child to participate and succeed, whatever their starting point.
Through a carefully sequenced curriculum, pupils develop their skills in drawing, painting, sculpture and other creative techniques. They build an understanding of colour, line, shape, form, texture and pattern, exploring how different materials and processes can communicate ideas. Opportunities to revisit and refine their work help children develop control, use artistic vocabulary confidently and reflect on their own and others’ creations.
Children encounter a diverse range of artists, craftspeople and designers from different cultures and periods, broadening their horizons and understanding of the world. Through experimentation and creative choices, they develop curiosity, perseverance and the courage to take risks. We want every child to leave our school with the skills, confidence and enthusiasm to create art and a lasting appreciation of human creativity.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Design and Technology
pageCache.text:
Design and Technology
At Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School, our Design and Technology curriculum aims to develop confident, creative problem-solvers who can design, make and evaluate purposeful products. Through this practical and ambitious subject, all children are encouraged to become bold and courageous learners, using imagination, technical knowledge and practical skills to respond to real needs.
Our carefully sequenced curriculum builds children’s understanding of materials, mechanisms, structures, textiles, food and nutrition. Pupils investigate, design, make, evaluate and refine their creations, revisiting key knowledge and techniques as they progress through the school. Meaningful design challenges encourage them to experiment, learn from mistakes and develop resilience.
Children learn to communicate their ideas through discussion, technical vocabulary, annotated sketches and written evaluations. They consider how products work, who they are for and how they could be improved, developing the confidence to explain and justify their decisions.
By the time they leave our school, pupils will have the knowledge, skills and confidence to approach practical challenges creatively and independently. They will understand how design and technology shapes everyday life and see themselves as designers, makers and innovators who can contribute responsibly to the world around them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Wraparound Care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
We are pleased to be able to offer wraparound care for children attending Walberton & Binsted CE Primary School through Community Playcentre @ Walberton. (CPAWS)
The Playcentre provides both Breakfast Club and After School Club, giving families flexible childcare before and after the school day.
Breakfast Club runs from 7.30am to 8.50am and includes a choice of cereals, toast, preserves and fruit.
After School Club runs from 3.15pm to 6.00pm. Children are offered fruit and a drink on arrival, with a hot meal provided later in the session.
Places are booked directly through Community Playcentre @ Walberton. Current fees, booking forms and further information are available on their website:
Visit Community Playcentre @ Walberton – Out of School Club
For enquiries, please contact the Playcentre directly on 01243 931848 or email accounts@communityplaycentre.org

pageCache.pageTitle: Walberton and Binsted C.E Primary School - Early Years (EYFS)
pageCache.text:
The Early Years
A strong start
We want every child to begin school feeling safe, valued and excited to learn. Our Reception year combines warm relationships, purposeful play and carefully planned teaching, helping children develop the foundations for future success.
Our curriculum covers all seven areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage. Children build their knowledge in manageable steps, with time to practise, revisit and grow in confidence.
Learning through play
Play is central to our approach. Through exploring, building, imagining and investigating, children develop ideas, solve problems and learn to work together.
Our carefully planned continuous provision (the resources and activities children can return to throughout the day) encourages independence and helps them practise their learning. Adults adapt and extend opportunities as children’s understanding develops.
Our outdoor area is an important part of the classroom, offering space for movement, discovery and larger-scale play. Children develop coordination, explore the natural world and tackle practical challenges together.
Stories and language
Thoughtful interactions help children make sense of their experiences. Adults listen closely, introduce vocabulary and encourage children to explain their thinking, making sure quieter children have opportunities to contribute.
Stories, songs and rhymes are woven into each day. Revisiting favourites develops language, memory and the pleasure of joining in.
Our 'Drawing Club' approach brings stories to life through conversation, imagination, drawing and early writing. Children create characters and adventures, developing confidence in expressing and recording their ideas.
Alongside this, Little Wandle phonics teaches early reading systematically. Practical mathematics develops understanding of number, pattern, shape and space.
Routines and relationships
Predictable routines help children feel settled and understand what happens next. We teach children how to use resources, care for belongings, take turns and manage everyday tasks. Calm, consistent support helps them understand feelings, build friendships and persevere.
We work closely with families, building on each child’s strengths and identifying additional support or challenge. Our aim is for every child to leave Reception with secure foundations, growing independence and enthusiasm for the next stage of learning.
At the end of the Reception year, getting the move to Year 1 right really matters to us. Learn about our approach to transition.
